s1.syndrome_frame: progressive radicular pain and neuropathic symptoms in the lower extremity
salient_findings: radicular pain radiating from lower back down the left leg
mild hypesthesia in the left L5–S1 dermatome
cystic mass in the left L5–S1 foraminal zone extending along the course of the sciatic nerve
key_facts: 8-month history of radicular pain
pain radiates from lower back down the left leg
occasional tingling
no weakness or autonomic symptoms
no history of trauma or injury
mild hypesthesia in the left L5–S1 dermatome
normal muscle strength
electromyography showed neuropathic irritation of the left L4, L5, S1, and S2 roots
lumbosacral MRI revealed a solitary, completely cystic mass in the left L5–S1 foraminal zone
mass measures approximately 13.9 cm in length and 1.9 cm in maximal diameter
mass is hypointense on T1-weighted images and hyperintense on T2-weighted images

shortlist.label: schwannoma
shortlist.why_kept: cystic mass along the course of the sciatic nerve with peripheral rim enhancement on MRI

shortlist.label: neurofibroma
shortlist.why_kept: solitary, completely cystic mass in the left L5–S1 foraminal zone extending along the course of the sciatic nerve

shortlist.label: perineurioma
shortlist.why_kept: progressive radicular pain and neuropathic symptoms with a cystic mass on MRI

shortlist.label: tarlov cyst
shortlist.why_kept: cystic mass in the L5–S1 foraminal zone with hyperintensity on T2-weighted images

shortlist.label: malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor
shortlist.why_kept: large size of the cystic mass and severe foraminal stenosis

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of radicular pain and tingling, along with the MRI findings of a solitary, completely cystic mass arising from the sciatic nerve, is most consistent with a schwannoma. The mass's characteristics on MRI, including its hypointensity on T1-weighted images and hyperintensity on T2-weighted images, as well as its peripheral rim enhancement, are also typical of a schwannoma.

rejected.label: neurofibroma
rejected.why: While neurofibromas can also present as cystic masses, they are less likely to cause severe foraminal stenosis and are often associated with other neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1) symptoms, which are not mentioned in the case.

rejected.label: perineurioma
rejected.why: Perineuriomas are rare tumors that can cause nerve damage, but they are not typically characterized by a cystic appearance on MRI.

rejected.label: tarlov cyst
rejected.why: Tarlov cysts are fluid-filled sacs that can compress nerves, but they are usually located in the spinal canal and do not typically extend along the course of a nerve like the sciatic nerve.

rejected.label: malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor
rejected.why: Malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumors are aggressive tumors that can cause significant nerve damage, but they are less common than schwannomas and often have a more heterogeneous appearance on MRI.
